items.title: Measuring the pace of AI development inside frontier labs
items.summary: A lab publishing a number on how much of its own research its model now runs — and, more usefully, the method it used to get there.

_homepage.note: Anthropic built an R&D Automation Index by cataloguing every kind of AI research task done internally, rating each against Epoch AI's AL0–AL5 automation scale, and weighting by how much staff time each consumes. The headline figure is that Claude now 'leads' — completes end-to-end from a high-level prompt, under supervision — 26 percent of that work, up from effectively zero in February. The measurement framework is the transferable part: the same catalogue-rate-weight structure is how you would honestly assess where AI sits in any clinical workflow, rather than arguing from demos.

items.title: SGEM#520: Morphine, but do I need to add acetaminophen?
items.summary: A noninferiority trial on IV paracetamol alongside morphine that failed to show noninferiority without showing benefit either — the kind of result that gets misread in both directions.

_homepage.note: The Cattin trial randomised ED patients in acute pain to morphine plus placebo or morphine plus IV acetaminophen, and morphine alone was not shown to be noninferior — which is not the same as acetaminophen having earned its place. Guest skeptic is Caitlin Jones from Sydney University's Institute for Musculoskeletal Health, whose research is specifically on the harms of opioid prescribing for musculoskeletal pain, so the appraisal is pitched at an Australian prescribing context rather than a North American one. Worth reading before the next time a multimodal analgesia protocol gets waved at you on shift.

items.title: Momotaro Jeans Stitched Up a Lightweight Sashiko Work Shirt
items.summary: A clean explanation of why almost nothing sold as sashiko is actually sashiko, hung off a shirt you could wear in a Melbourne spring.

_homepage.note: The useful part is the terminology: sashiko proper is the reinforcing running stitch, while fabrics like this are sashiko-ori, woven on a dobby loom to imitate that stitch pattern. Momotaro's MMLS6018 is indigo rope-dyed cotton cut deliberately light — a layer rather than an overshirt, which is the gap most heritage chore-coat-adjacent pieces miss. Sits directly next to the chore coat and bleu de travail material already in the feed.

items.title: Witcher 3 Remastered hits PS5 and PS5 Pro as a free upgrade
items.summary: Free on 29 September if you already own it on PS5, with both expansions included and the combat system actually reworked rather than re-lit.

_homepage.note: CD Projekt Red worked with Hungarian co-developer Yigsoft to rebuild the rendering pipeline outright, and the changes go past resolution — reworked combat, a restructured skill tree, and Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine bundled in. No charge for existing PS5 owners, which makes the decision a download rather than a purchase. It also lands two months before GTA 6, so it is a finite thing to finish rather than something to start.

items.title: Police say young people are stashing knives across Melbourne
items.summary: Victoria Police intelligence obtained by the ABC suggests the machete ban has pushed underage offenders toward concealing weapons in public places.

_homepage.note: A year after the machete ban came in, internal police briefs say the unintended consequence is caching — knives hidden in parks and around shopping precincts rather than carried. The same week produced arrests over a brawl at Northland in Preston, which is the northside end of this rather than an abstract policy story. Penetrating trauma in under-18s is the downstream version of this reporting, so it is worth knowing what the pattern actually is rather than what the headlines say it is.

items.title: Emergency Evidence Updates – August 2026
items.summary: A month of ED-relevant papers appraised in short form, including physiotherapy-performed trauma tertiary surveys and paediatric e-scooter injuries.

_homepage.note: The Bottom Line is better known for its critical care trial appraisals, but the emergency stream is the one that maps onto a registrar's actual caseload — this month covers neurodiversity and violence-related attendances in Welsh EDs, dexmedetomidine for sedation, the WHO Hospital Emergency Unit Assessment Tool, and the e-scooter injury pattern that everyone's department is now seeing. Each entry is a paragraph and a verdict rather than a full appraisal, which makes it a scan-and-flag list rather than a read. This source hasn't appeared in the feed before.

items.title: Menahan Street Band announce new album 'Illusions'
items.summary: First Menahan record in over a decade, with Arthur Verocai writing the strings — which is a very different proposition to another Brooklyn soul instrumental album.

_homepage.note: Illusions lands 13 November on Tommy Brenneck's own Diamond West, twenty years after the band formed in his Bushwick apartment and became Charles Bradley's backing group. The lead track 'Palace of Illusions' carries string arrangements by Arthur Verocai, the Brazilian composer whose 1972 self-titled album is one of the most expensively traded records of the era; Brenneck describes it as pushing the horns somewhere they have not been. Menahan is already on the shelf here, and this is the one to pre-order rather than wait on.

items.title: New vinyl reissues: September 11, 2026
items.summary: A weekly reissue column that names the cutting engineer and the pressing plant, which is the only detail that separates a good reissue from a bad one.

_homepage.note: This week's headline is Ann Peebles' Tellin' It from 1975 — Hi Records Memphis soul, out of print for half a century — reissued by Fat Possum and pressed at Memphis Record Pressing, which is about as close to home as that record can get. The column's value is that it tracks mastering source and plant week by week rather than just announcing titles, so you can tell whether something was cut from tape or from a file before you commit. A source the feed hasn't used before, and a better fit for the soul end of the collection than the audiophile-boxset coverage.

items.title: Jagex working 'flat out' on Dragonwilds corrupted saves
items.summary: Console players lost whole worlds after the 1.0 launch, and the first hotfix only partly closed it — back up before you play.

_homepage.note: Dragonwilds left early access on 15 September and immediately started eating world saves on exit. The hotfix that followed addressed the corruption on exit plus a Great Body Robbery dialogue soft-lock and persistent agility times, but Jagex was still chasing worlds vanishing from the world list. Dedicated servers need a restart to take the fix, which matters if you are hosting rather than playing solo.

items.title: ORWO TF-12D — Controlling Contrast
items.summary: How to pull usable mid-tones out of an emulsion that was never designed to give you any.

_homepage.note: TF-12D is one of the ORWO technical stocks that shooters keep buying because it is cheap and sharp, then abandoning because straight development gives soot-and-chalk. This is the development-side answer — dilution and agitation as contrast controls rather than a fixed recipe — and it is the sort of piece that pays off on any high-contrast film, not just this one. Posted today.

items.title: ECG Pointers: STEMI Case Conference
items.summary: ECGs walked through against the angiograms that followed them, which is the only feedback loop that actually improves a reader.

_homepage.note: The ECG Pointers series runs cases where the tracing is presented, called, and then checked against what the cath lab found — the correlation step that almost never gets closed when you send a patient off the floor and never hear back. This instalment is a case conference format rather than a single tracing, so it covers several presentations and the reasoning that separated them. emDOCs hasn't appeared in the feed before and the ECG series is the strongest reason to add it.

items.title: Bar Elsie Makes You Want To Stay a While
items.summary: A European bistro at the top of Lygon Street built by two people who deliberately downsized after a near-fatal cardiac arrest.

_homepage.note: Brett and Susie Pritchard ran Arcadia Liquors, Redfern Continental and Ron's Upstairs in Sydney until Brett's cardiac arrest in 2022, sold the lot, and moved to Melbourne — The Coffee Bar first, then Bar Elsie in the same building at 396 Lygon Street, Brunswick East. Brett built the U-shaped bar himself, and the room is set up so a bowl of chips and a glass of wine is as legitimate as a full sitting. A short ride up from Tenko and Better Now on the same stretch.
